result.reason: All 6 immutable criteria are MET and harness compliance is clean, but one scope-honesty defect caps the verdict. Deterministic: immutable command `pytest backend/tests/test_phase_83_0_3_pbo_false_pass.py -q` -> 5 passed in 2.48s, bare exit=0 (re-run twice); regression 45 passed in 8.62s (reproduces the claimed 45/8.72s; 45 progress dots, internally consistent); ruff F821,F401,F811 over a git-DERIVED non-empty scope (1 file, xargs -0) -> "All checks passed!" exit=0; runtime smoke `import backend.agents.mcp_servers.risk_server, backend.backtest.analytics` -> OK; secret scan clean; NO unintended production change (git diff --name-only HEAD = only handoff/audit/*.jsonl hook streams; production code byte-unchanged as contract D1 claims). I ran an INDEPENDENT 9-mutant matrix in-memory (zero writes; md5 of both mutation targets unchanged after): CONTROL green; M1 drop T<S*2 refusal -> 2 failed at _assert_refusal L69 `r["ok"] is False`; M2 columns_diverse=always-True -> L145; M3 always-False -> mirror guard L157; M4 drop gate_grade key -> L149+L161; M5 loosen 0.99->0.9999 -> L145; H1 reword routing kwarg->positional -> L105 anchor `assert n == 1`; H2 degrade C4 fixture eps 0.0005->0.002 -> fails as a FIXTURE at the L139 precondition (assert 0.95465 > 0.99), exactly as designed. All killed, including the fixture/harness-side shapes. THE FINDING (impostor probe): contract D1 and the test docstring claim criterion 1 is "proven BEHAVIOURALLY (refusal on undersized input, which raw compute_pbo cannot produce)". I measured that false by construction -- I built a pbo_check doing its OWN inline T<S*2 refusal and calling RAW compute_pbo, never touching compute_pbo_checked, and ALL FOUR behavioural tests PASSED; only test_c3's literal source anchor (L104-108) caught it. Criterion 1 is therefore met, but by a mechanism the artifacts misattribute (qa.md 4c vacuity shape #11). The anchor is NOT itself vacuous -- I checked the dangerous direction: it cannot go green while routing is broken (reword -> count 0 -> red; a pathological docstring copy leaves the real call intact so L118 `r_mut["ok"] is True` goes red), and it is not comment-satisfiable (requires the 12-space-indented assignment). Forward risk is concrete: a maintainer reading D1 would judge the anchor redundant and delete it, silently zeroing criterion 1's only routing coverage. WARN -> CONDITIONAL per severity dispatch, not FAIL. Cycle 1 for 83.0.3 (no prior verdicts), so the 3rd-CONDITIONAL auto-FAIL rule is not triggered.

violation_details.state: IMPOSTOR rc=1: 1 failed, 4 passed. The 4 PASSING tests are test_c1_c2_undersized_matrix_refuses_not_passes, test_c4_near_identical_columns_reported_not_diverse, test_c4_mirror_independent_columns_reported_diverse, test_refusal_survives_client_round_trip -- i.e. every behavioural guard. The ONLY kill was test_c3 at L106: 'AssertionError: mutation anchor count=0, want exactly 1'. Corroborated by mutant H1 (routing text reworded kwarg->positional): same single kill at L105. So the claim in contract_83.0.3.md D1 ('Criterion-1 is proven BEHAVIOURALLY (refusal on undersized input, which raw compute_pbo cannot produce)') and the identical claim in the test docstring C1 (lines 8-11) are false as stated: raw compute_pbo CAN produce a refusal when wrapped inline, so refusal-observed does not entail routed-through-compute_pbo_checked.
violation_details.constraint: SEVERITY WARN (a genuine behavioural guard coexists, so this forces CONDITIONAL rather than FAIL per the severity-dispatch table). Rule: qa.md 4c guard-vacuity / vacuity shape #11 (mis-attributed kill mechanism -- 'name WHICH assertion killed') plus 4b claim-auditing (every scope claim in the handoff is an assertion to be REPRODUCED, not read). Criterion 1 ('pbo_check routes through compute_pbo_checked rather than compute_pbo, asserted by a test') IS satisfied -- test_c3 L104-108 `assert src.count(_ORIG) == 1` is a genuine, non-vacuous routing guard that fires -- but the artifacts credit the wrong mechanism. NAMED FIX: (a) correct D1 and the test docstring to credit the test_c3 anchor as criterion 1's routing discriminator and state that the behavioural refusal is necessary-but-not-sufficient (an inline-refusal impostor passes all four behavioural tests); (b) add a 'do not delete: this is criterion 1's only routing guard' comment at L104-108; (c) optionally add a direct routing spy (monkeypatch backend.backtest.analytics.compute_pbo_checked and assert it was called) so routing becomes behaviourally observable rather than text-anchored.

C5 MET -- my independent AST census used a BROADER rule than the author's (func.id OR func.attr) and reproduced the same 5 sites with EMPTY symmetric difference: analytics.py:240 (wrapper delegation), test_phase_82_23:37, test_phase_83_0_3:86 (new), run_82_3_candidate_backtests.py:206, tests/autoresearch/test_phase_48_2:106. NOTE-level, non-capping. With `--include='*.py'` it returns EXACTLY 50. The number is right, the transcription drops the qualifier; since criterion 5 names "committed grep output", commit the qualified form. N2 Guard line-numbers off by ~6: experiment_results:33 says run_82_3_candidate_backtests.py:206 is "guarded at :195/:203"; the actual guard conditions are `if len(series) < 2:` at :192 and `if T < 32:` at :200 (:195/:203 are note-string lines inside those blocks).
